title: Build Trustworthy Analytics with dbt and Defend It

teaser.setup: You own the transformation layer. Stakeholders don't trust the numbers and full refreshes are slow and expensive. Design a dbt project and defend the calls — project structure, testing, incremental models, and CI.
you_will_practice: Tests, contracts, and freshness as quality gates

sample_node.prompt: How do you stop a bad column or broken join from reaching a mart?
sample_node.model: dbt tests as gates: not_null/unique on keys, relationships for referential integrity, accepted_values for enums, and source freshness. Add model contracts on exposed marts so types/columns can't drift. Run build+test in CI on every PR and block merge on failure. Quarantine or fail rather than publish silently.

n1.prompt: Clarify first, then give your one-paragraph dbt design for trustworthy, affordable marts.
n1.model: Clarify: sources + grain, which metrics are authoritative, freshness SLO, and the cost of full refresh. Design: layered models — staging (1:1 source cleanup) → intermediate → marts, all via ref() not hard-coded tables; tests + contracts + source freshness as gates; incremental materialization where refresh is expensive; docs/lineage from the DAG; CI runs build+test on PRs. One semantic definition per metric.
signals: tests + contracts + CI as the trust mechanism

n2.prompt: Why a staging layer instead of writing marts directly off raw sources?
n2.model: Staging isolates source-specific cleanup (renames, types, dedup) so marts depend on a stable internal shape, not on raw quirks. When a source changes you fix one staging model, not every mart. It also makes lineage and testing clear. Trade-off: more models to maintain — worth it for change isolation and trust.
signals: change in one place, not every mart

n3.prompt: How do you stop a bad column or broken join from reaching a mart?
n3.model: dbt tests as gates: not_null/unique on keys, relationships for referential integrity, accepted_values for enums, source freshness. Add model contracts on exposed marts so types/columns can't drift. Run build+test in CI on every PR and block merge on failure. Fail or quarantine rather than publish silently.

n4.prompt: Full refreshes are too slow and expensive. How do you make models incremental safely?
n4.model: Incremental materialization with a stable unique_key and an is_incremental() filter on a watermark. Use merge (or delete+insert) so reruns converge — no duplicates. Handle late-arriving data with a lookback window. Keep a full-refresh path for logic changes/backfills, and test that the incremental result equals the full result on a sample. Idempotent by design.
signals: lookback for late data + full-refresh escape hatch

n5.prompt: Two dashboards show different revenue numbers. Diagnose and fix the trust problem.
n5.model: Root cause is usually a metric defined twice with different logic/filters. Find the canonical definition, move it into ONE dbt model (or a semantic/metrics layer), and point both dashboards at it. Add a test asserting the metric's expected properties. The fix is a single source of truth for the metric, not reconciling two queries by hand each time.

n6.prompt: Where did you assert a choice without the mechanism, the trade-off, or the verification?
checklist: I layered staging→marts for change isolation
I gated trust with tests + contracts + CI, not hope
I made incremental models idempotent (merge + lookback)
I fixed divergent numbers with one canonical metric definition

recommend.label: Keep Asking Why — data platform chain
